subject: Private connectivity: egress ownership, firewall owners, and PrivateLink clarifications
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@oakridge.com>
Cc: Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@oakridge.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private connectivity: egress ownership, firewall owners, and PrivateLink clarifications

Hi Laura / Aaron —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our end and a handful of follow-ups so we can scope the Private VPC option correctly (PrivateLink vs VPC peering):

Key decisions we need to confirm:
- Deployment preference: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC (you mentioned Private VPC + PrivateLink as preferred). Please confirm final preference.
- Egress model: Do you require fixed egress IPs from Redwood (we can provide a small range) or will you route egress through your NAT/proxy? Which team owns firewall rules on your side?
- Network details we need: VPC CIDR, subnets for PrivateLink endpoints, any forced-tunnel/proxy requirements, and DNS expectations.
- Security checklist: SOC 2 evidence, audit log retention, KMS integration — I attached your preflight questionnaire as a copy for tracking.

Action items (for scope + timeline):
1) Oakridge: confirm deployment preference and who will own egress firewall rules (network ops contact).
2) Oakridge: share VPC CIDR and whether you prefer PrivateLink (endpoint in your VPC) or classic peering.
3) Redwood (Ben): produce proposed egress IP ranges and recommended NAT/proxy configuration for PrivateLink.
4) Redwood (Marissa): open HubSpot deal record and add procurement/PO timeline.

Next step — if you confirm PrivateLink as the path, Ben will produce the allowlist IPs and a short network diagram; we can then schedule a 30-min network ops call to finalize firewall rules.

Attachment: Oakridge_preflight_questions.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0183

-----

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@oakridge.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@oakridge.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 16:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private connectivity: egress ownership, firewall owners, and PrivateLink clarifications

Thanks Irene — good recap. Confirming: Oakridge prefers Private VPC with PrivateLink endpoints. A few clarifications from our security/network team:

- We need a stable set of egress IPs that we can add to our outbound allowlist (SOC requires documented ranges). If Redwood can provide a /29 or similar that's ideal.
- Firewall ownership: Oakridge network ops will control inbound rules on our side. We expect Redwood to be responsible for any egress originating from your infrastructure (i.e., if you originate callbacks).
- VPC CIDR: 10.240.0.0/16 (we'll provide exact subnets once we confirm).
- We have an outbound proxy for internet egress; prefer to avoid double-NAT. If Redwood can route egress back through our proxy during initial setup, that would be helpful.

I'll attach the prefilled preflight; Aaron will be the network contact for the ops call.

Attachment: Oakridge_preflight_questions.pdf (filled)

Regards,
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Infrastructure | Oakridge Payments
laura.chen@oakridge.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private connectivity: egress ownership, firewall owners, and PrivateLink clarifications

Folks — forwarding the customer confirmation. High level ask: provide egress IP proposal and recommend egress pattern (Redwood-provided fixed IPs vs routing through customer proxy). Also flag any constraints for PrivateLink (MTU, TLS SNI, DNS override) we should share back to Oakridge.

Please add notes below with owners and ETA. I want to lock technical scope by EOD Wednesday so procurement can start.

Irene

-----

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private connectivity: egress ownership, firewall owners, and PrivateLink clarifications

Thanks Irene — taking this on. Quick answers / plan:

1) Egress IPs: We can allocate a small static range for callbacks and outbound connections from our side. Initial proposal attached (redwood-egress-ip-proposal.xlsx). Typical allocation is a /29 (8 IPs) which covers high-availability NAT plus spare. If Oakridge needs fewer, we can shrink.
2) Egress routing options:
   - Option A (recommended for simplest ops): Redwood provides fixed egress IPs and we advertise those as the source for any outbound traffic. Oakridge add those to your allowlist. This avoids additional proxy config on your side.
   - Option B: Route calls back through Oakridge proxy (Redwood egress via customer proxy). Works but requires configuring mutual TLS for proxy auth in front of our connectors and additional e2e testing.
3) PrivateLink notes: MTU shouldn't be an issue for standard AWS PrivateLink. DNS: we'll need SRV / CNAME guidance if you plan to override names in your VPC. TLS: we support SNI and cert pinning for endpoint verification.

ETA: I'll produce a final IP range proposal and diagram by Wed 2026-08-11 10:00 PT. Please confirm Oakridge's preference for Option A vs B.

Ben Carter
Network Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-egress-ip-proposal.xlsx (xlsx)

-----

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private connectivity: egress ownership, firewall owners, and PrivateLink clarifications

Great — thanks Laura and Ben.

Summary / confirmed next steps:
- Oakridge confirms Private VPC + PrivateLink.
- Oakridge network ops (Aaron) will own inbound firewall rules; Oakridge to provide exact subnet list.
- Redwood (Ben) to deliver proposed /29 egress range and a short diagram by Wed 2026-08-11 10:00 PT.
- Decision on egress mode: Oakridge to confirm Option A (Redwood-provided IPs) vs Option B (proxy backhaul) by Tue 2026-08-10 EOD.
- Marissa to prepare procurement timeline and contract milestone in HubSpot; I'll follow up with a 30-min ops call link.

Scheduling link: https://redwood.app/schedule/irene-30m
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

I'll mark these action items in the deal and loop in security for SOC 2 evidence once the network plan is final.

Thanks all,
Irene
